$comment: Ratcheted ceilings on the surfaces this campaign exists to shrink.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The campaign produced 132 plan documents and one
mechanism that never failed: EXPECTED_HOST_IMPORT_COUNT, a number in the
repo asserted against a measurement of the built artifact. Every import
change hit it. Meanwhile fork TypeScript grew by 2,867 lines over the same
period with nothing to catch it, and nobody noticed for weeks. Documents
are advisory; a number a test asserts is not.
HOW THE RATCHET WORKS. Exceeding a ceiling fails: the surface grew.
Falling more than `slack` below it ALSO fails, asking you to lower the
ceiling in the same commit. That is what banks a reduction permanently --
without it, one lane's deletion silently funds the next lane's growth.
WHAT A CEILING IS NOT. It is not a goal. Every `target` below is far under
its ceiling, and the gap is the work. See docs/plans/2026-09-11-MASTER-PLAN.md.
LANE CLOSURE. `lanes` below binds each lane's status to measurements. A lane
marked `closed` whose conditions are unmet fails; a lane marked `open` whose
conditions are all met ALSO fails, saying to close it. Lane status therefore
cannot be asserted in prose -- which is what every previous attempt did, and
why drift was only ever caught when a human happened to ask.
A lane whose completion is not a number says so with `manual` and a reason.
That is honest; silence is not.
CHECKLIST CLOSURE is weaker than a measurement and is labelled as such. A
tick is self-reported. Its value is that the instances are enumerated, so a
lane cannot be closed by forgetting one.
CHARACTERIZATION is gated too. A lane must carry an End state, a floor, an
Increments list, Acceptance evidence and Known hazards before it is
dispatchable. A lane legitimately missing one declares `sectionsExempt` with
a reason -- because the failure this file exists to end is a status asserted
in prose that nothing checks, and that applies to its own sections first.

forkGuestImportsUnserved.measure: canonical fork imports in the crates/shared ProgramArtifactImport table that crates/fork-module does not export under the same name
forkGuestImportsUnserved.why:
The guest declares 46 fork imports. Each one the fork-module exports VERBATIM can be wired with a nameless loop -- host-native already does this for the five frame imports. Each one exported under a different spelling (fm_ref_gc_route for __wpk_fork_ref_gc_route) forces a mapping table back into the host, which is the hand-maintained-knowledge-beside-a-generator defect three censuses in this campaign have found. Target 0 is the point at which the JS host layer is pure wiring. The 19 -> 18 step, banked 2026-09-12, is __wpk_fork_ref_exn_define: the one define in the family that needs nothing but guest linear memory, because fork-instrument's exception codec stages scalars AND the payload recipe ids into a single scratch span before the call. GROUNDED BREAKDOWN of the remaining 18, read at each emission site in crates/fork-instrument rather than inferred from signatures: 5 are the module_state_table_* mutation group, blocked on an undefined journal format (maintainer decision). Of the other 13: TWO need no new fm_* entry at all (gc_define and gc_provenance_end are pure scalars over guest memory) but both are coupled to the provenance registry and must land with it -- serving gc_define alone would bake in 'provenance is always absent', which is only true because nothing serves provenance_begin yet. TEN each need an injected wasm shim backed by a new fm_* helper: seven because the value arrives in a reference-typed TABLE slot (gc_capture_layout, gc_broker_encode, gc_provenance_begin, gc_provenance_ref, exn_lookup, exn_claim, exn_broker_encode), two because they must THROW so the guest's try_table catches the exnref -- the emitter puts `unreachable` after the call, so returning normally is a bug (exn_ingress_throw, exn_broker_throw_recipe) -- and one because it is externref in and externref out (provenance_externref). The LAST one, encode_funcref, is the only remaining import that grows the HOST contract: it takes the funcref as a parameter and must return its recipe id, wasm cannot compare funcrefs, and funcref is not a subtype of anyref, so the approved __wpk_fork_host_ref_identity cannot serve it -- it needs a funcref-identity host import of its own. So the tranche is about +11 fm_ entries against a ceiling of 54, plus one new host import. That collision is what has to be resolved before it can land. The 18 -> 15 step, banked 2026-09-12, is the constructor-provenance trio (__wpk_fork_ref_gc_provenance_begin/_ref/_end). begin and end are pure scalars and needed no shim at all; only _ref does, because it moves the guest's staged seed from the transit table into a module-owned WITNESS table. Crucially it needs no host import and no reference identity: the witness is keyed by (layout, ordinal), both plain integers the guest already passes, which is what keeps it off the allocation hot path. See docs/plans/2026-09-12-lane-f-census.md sections 21 and 22. The 15 -> 13 step, banked 2026-09-12, is __wpk_fork_ref_exn_lookup and __wpk_fork_ref_exn_claim, both pure Rust with no shim and no host surface. Lookup always reports NOT FOUND, so every catch takes a fresh recipe. That is a measured decision, not a shortcut: NOTHING can dedup an exception. Wasm cannot -- `exn` is a disjoint hierarchy, so ref.eq on two exnrefs does not validate, an exnref cannot enter an anyref table, and no cast rescues one into the eq hierarchy; only ref.is_null accepts an exnref at all. And a JS host cannot -- an exnref VALUE cannot cross into a JS import, which compiles and instantiates then throws TypeError at the first call. The same limitation is why it costs nothing: a guest cannot observe that two exnrefs are distinct either, and payloads still dedup through the normal identity path, so two exception recipes share their payload objects. Measured with wasm-tools validate against a positive AND a negative control; see census sections 28a, 28b and 29. The 13 -> 12 step is __wpk_fork_ref_exn_broker_encode, the unknown-tag path, served as a LOUD REFUSAL: EOPNOTSUPP and a poisoned recipe. A foreign exception is opaque on every axis -- its payload needs catch_ref against a tag this module does not have, it cannot be identified, and it cannot be handed to a host to inspect. Real handling means routing to the activation whose codec owns the tag, which needs a capture-side drive that does not exist (F3). The refusal is structural rather than a gated placeholder BECAUSE no gate signal is exported -- fm_stats has no gated counter -- so a placeholder would let the child rebuild the i31(0) sentinel where an exception had been and say nothing. The poisoned value is not a valid recipe id, so any edge naming it is rejected at define and the capture cannot seal. That restriction (no fork while a foreign exception is live) is stated, not hidden, and is not a regression: an unserved import leaves the same case to a host that cannot inspect the exception either. Census section 30. The 12 -> 11 step is __wpk_fork_ref_gc_define, and it is the first time the module DRIVES THE GUEST to capture rather than to replay. Constructor-provenance witnesses are interned lazily inside it, through an injected shim that stages the witness in the anyref transit slot and call_indirects the guest's own __wpk_fork_ref_gc_encode_slot at drive slot 11 -- so the module gets a recipe for a reference Rust can neither hold nor describe. The recipe is CACHED per witness, since a witness is shared by every object of its layout. §21 established gc_define must not be served without this: alone it would pass no provenance for every object and bake in 'provenance is always absent'. No host import was added and no target-0 ceiling moved -- the shim is reached through the placeholder-import pattern, so the emitted module carries no unresolved import. Census sections 38, 39, 40 and 41. The 11 -> 10 step is __wpk_fork_ref_gc_capture_layout, answered by driving the guest's own TYPE-TEST probe at drive slot 12 rather than by keeping a map. A layout is a per-OBJECT fact -- two objects of one base type can be made by different constructors -- so the witness trick that made provenance bounded does not apply, and recording it per object is the unbounded storage problem of census §20. Asking the guest costs nothing and stores nothing: the value is already in the transit slot and the guest's generated codec ref.tests it, returning (type_ordinal << 32) | layout_id. The caller's static layout argument is deliberately NOT trusted over the type test. Census §42. The 10 -> 9 step is __wpk_fork_ref_gc_broker_encode, the cross-activation path: a structurally canonical GC value can enter through another dynamically loaded module, whose codec is the one that can encode it. The module cannot inspect a reference, so it ASKS each registered activation's codec through the drive table and routes to the first CLAIMANT -- probe then encode, both the guest's own generated functions. Bounded by the number of registered activations, not by objects. An unclaimed value is EOPNOTSUPP and a poisoned recipe rather than an invented one, the same structural refusal the exception broker uses. Census §43.

BANKED 4 -> 3 on 2026-09-13. `table_state_owned` moved into the module. The host still ELECTS which coordinate owns a physical table -- that compares `WebAssembly.Table` object identity, which wasm cannot do -- but it now SEEDS the result through `fm_set_activation_table_state_owner` instead of answering a callback per call, and the module serves the guest import from what it was told. Electing and answering were two jobs in one host function; only the first needs JavaScript.

What remains is three, and all three are arguable rather than pending: the two `exn_*` throws the maintainer deferred (a JS import cannot re-enter wasm THROWING a tagged exception) and `provenance_externref` (reads a handle off a token and keys a map by object identity). This surface's target of 0 assumes all three eventually move; that assumption is now the whole remaining distance.

forkModuleInjectorHelpers.measure:
fm_* entries called ONLY by crates/fork-module-inject (an injected wasm shim), never by a host
BANKED 3 -> 2 on 2026-09-16: `__wpk_fork_resume_table`. It was argued as host floor in `fork-guest-imports.ts`, in these words -- "Rust cannot hold a funcref, and the module's `resume_peek` returns an index INTO this table, so it has to exist outside the module" -- and the conclusion does not follow from the premise. Rust cannot hold a funcref; the INJECTOR can declare a funcref table, exactly as it already declares the anyref transit table, and the module exports it. Nothing has to HOLD a funcref for a table to exist. The host now takes the table from `moduleExports` like the transit table and the unwind tag, and `ForkResumeTable` only fills it -- which also means the guest's import, the module's numbering and the host's placement are one object rather than a per-caller convention. The two left are genuinely the host's: `__wpk_fork_module_activation` is per-activation and one module instance serves every activation, and the generation-fence address is a per-process placement.
TARGET RESTATED 0 -> 2 on 2026-09-16, by maintainer decision, after asking what ABI change would close it -- we are mid-epoch, so an ABI change is cheap right now. The answer for both is that no ABI change helps, and the reasons are different from the one recorded in census 199. `__wpk_fork_module_state_table_generation_addr`: the width mismatch was a RED HERRING. The fence lives at `dlopenArchiveControlAddr - offset`, inside the PROCESS-WIDE dlopen archive control region that every worker in the process shares -- and each worker has its own fork-module instance at its own `__memory_base`. A module-placed fence would be a different address per worker, which is the one thing it cannot be. `__wpk_fork_module_activation`: an ABI change DOES exist -- bind the eleven activation-id call sites through per-activation trampolines, as the six frame imports already are, and the argument and the global both disappear. It is not worth it: the host still binds a per-activation slice, so its work changes shape rather than going away, and the trampoline table grows from 6x64 to about 14x64 injected functions. Trading one `new WebAssembly.Global({value:'i32'}, id)` for ~500 more injected functions makes the artifact worse to close a number. Census 203.
forkModuleInjectorHelpers.why: Internal implementation, NOT host surface. Each exists because the work is split across a boundary neither side can cross alone: the injected wasm shim is the only thing that can HOLD a reference, and Rust is the only thing that can hold a MAP or a counter. The shim calls the host import to turn its reference into an integer, then calls into Rust with that integer. A host never sees these, so they add nothing a host must implement. Currently 3: fm_drive_bump, fm_gc_identity_find, fm_gc_identity_claim. B.title: build and provisioning truthfulness
B.why: Closure is that a build which cannot produce a usable artifact says so, and that the documented provisioning path and the documented freshness gate agree. Neither is a count.

T.title: test hygiene
T.why: Closure is every host-suite failure attributed to a named cause. Blocked on a clean suite read rather than on work.

H.title: browser
H.why: Deprioritized by the maintainer. Closure is a browser pass plus curation, both of which are judgement rather than measurement.
H.whyExempt: Deprioritized by the maintainer, who asked to push implementation further before paying the cost of browser verification. Characterizing it now would plan work nobody intends to start.

K.title: kernel-worker.ts — one god class every lane contends for
K.why: The K1 census corrected the lane's framing: this is NOT the host's second syscall table. The 85 syscalls it dispatches are the ones needing a host service — worker creation, Atomics.wait blocking, shared memory — and host-native dispatches the same set. The defect is shape: 522 methods in one class, 29,975 lines, against guest.rs's 13,577 for the same responsibility. DRIFT NOTE 2026-09-17: guest.rs is now 14,814 lines, not 13,577.

G.title: ABI binding drift — all 15 layout modules anchored to generated constants
G.why: A layout constant with no static assert on the C side can drift from what musl expects and nothing notices. statx is the proven instance; 9 of 15 modules are equally exposed.

D.title: dead Rust floors
D.why: Five dead Rust modules beyond shared_mapping_policy were found and never characterized. A count is the wrong measure because the answer per module is either 'give it a caller' or 'delete it', and both reduce the same number. SELF-REPORTED checklist; a tick is a claim.
D.whyExempt: Dead code has no capability boundary to describe; the floor question belongs to whichever lane owns the subsystem each module was written for.

L.title: Host-kernel plumbing — what a wasmtime host writes beyond the imports
L.why: Goal V1 more than V4, which the L1 census established: a new host's burden here is already near zero — host-native proves it — but the same knowledge exists twice and the second copy was made by transcription (62 comment blocks in host-native cite host/src/*.ts, measured 2026-09-13; the census said 47 — and of the 13 that carry a line number, 10 no longer resolve: 3 name a file deleted by ace9756b1, 2 name identifiers that no longer exist, and 5 are 100-200 lines off because the cited file grew). Two transcribed copies drift and host #3 transcribes a third. L2 aside, every increment landed 2026-09-13: L3 both halves, L4 and L5. The lane measures 5,689. L2 is DECLINED rather than blocked: its recorded premise is wrong, but the table is guarded by host/test/kernel-scratch-contract.test.ts and generating it buys line count without safety. The closure figure is NOT derived and is left at the census's 3,600 as a placeholder; see the surface's why.

E.title: Node/browser peer divergence — shared types unified to the audited floor
E.why: Goal V1. CLOSED 2026-09-12 at the floor the E3 audit derived. The consolidation was already largely done before the lane started — the worker-entry pair shares 72 lifecycle members through a createProcessLifecycle factory — and what remained was 36 duplicated protocol declarations, now unified. The floor of 29 is 21 worker-entry declarations that are legitimately per-host (4 module-state lets, 17 platform differences), 6 genuinely-different protocol types, and 2 message unions. No category-three divergence was ever found: no bug one host fixed and the other did not.

R.title: Binary and artifact resolution — one declaration of the tier order
R.why: Goal V1. Not a resolver migration: host-native reimplemented ten lines, not 4,020. The tier list and its order are spelled 8 times across the writer and both readers, and that drift has already produced a measured failure. The right fix was already applied once inside TypeScript (binary-tiers.ts) and stopped at the language boundary.

Y.title: VFS image builders write the image format in TypeScript
Y.why: Goal V3, and a hard prerequisite for lane V. The Y1 census found the Rust side already covers nearly the whole builder contract across sffs_write.rs, sffs.rs and sffs_deferred.rs; the gaps are six image-level operations and three policy assertions, not a filesystem. Not a line-reduction lane — a decoupling lane. CLOSED 2026-09-13 on its own stated condition: zero files under `images/` import `memory-fs` or `sharedfs-vendor`, down from 36. What closing does NOT mean: gap 21 is still open (a legacy image's standalone lazy file is re-exported as a zero-length ordinary file, pinned by an `it.fails` test), and the shipped base images have NOT yet been rebuilt through the Rust producer, which is what makes the seal real rather than inert. Both are tracked in the master plan; neither is measured by this surface, which is a decoupling measure and says only that the builders no longer reach the format through the TypeScript filesystem.

W.title: web-libs session contracts a new host consumes
W.why: Goals V1 and V2. The W1 census found three populations, not two: the host contract, the browser product surface that stays, and a third the lane missed — hand-written parsers of kernel-emitted /proc formats plus a hand-maintained syscall table that is 96 entries short of the generated one and disagrees with it on two names.

U.title: Build automation in shell and MJS
U.why: Goal V2 and the repo's Rust-tools preference. Still does NOT serve V4 and stays ranked last. But the U1 census separates a cheap tier-1 subset (one Rust digest primitive replacing two shell copies, plus the manifest emitter lane S already needs) with already-realised failure modes, from the tier-2 bulk the census recommends not migrating.

N.title: Committed binaries without producers
N.why: The maintainer's binaries policy, made enforceable. Not lane F's to own even though lane F's deletions make it urgent: F would be deciding the fate of fixtures that guard the code it is removing. The clock is set by THREE lanes, not one — F, V and Y are all deleting producers.
